briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Michigan Weed Hits $17B Milestone as Psychedelics Go Mainstream Nationally
briefs.top: Michigan's legal cannabis market just crossed $17 billion in lifetime sales even as the 24% wholesale tax becomes the defining issue of the governor's race, with both the industry and a leading candidate now aligned on repeal. Nationally, momentum is building fast on multiple fronts — FDA is fast-tracking psychedelic therapies, courts just upheld marijuana's Schedule III status, and Eli Lilly is putting real money behind next-gen mental health drugs.

local.text: Michigan cannabis market tops $17 billion lifetime — Combined adult-use and medical marijuana sales have surpassed $17 billion since legalization, per the CRA's newest monthly report, with August alone bringing in $259 million.

Industry group endorses GOP nominee over tax repeal — MiCIA officially backed John James for governor, with Executive Director Robin Schneider calling him "the clear choice for the cannabis industry" over his pledge to kill the 24% wholesale tax.

Muskegon hospitality dispensary build keeps moving forward — Fields Cannary's ambitious dispensary-restaurant concept is still on track for a fall opening, proof that hospitality-driven cannabis retail hasn't stalled despite industry headwinds.
Voting opens for Michigan's best weed brands — The MichiGanja Report launched its statewide brand awards ballot, with polls closing Sept. 30 and winners announced in October.

Tax revenue miss adds fuel to repeal push — The 24% wholesale tax generated just $37 million in Q2 against a $105 million-per-quarter projection, strengthening the case behind a bipartisan repeal bill and a second industry lawsuit headed to trial.

national.text: FDA advances roadmap for psychedelic therapies — The agency held a Sept. 14 public hearing on therapeutic psychedelics and issued its first final clinical-trial guidance for psilocybin, LSD and MDMA, its most concrete step yet under the April executive order.

Compass Pathways psilocybin nears FDA finish line — COMP360 could win approval by late 2026 for treatment-resistant depression, positioning it as the first psychedelic drug reviewed under the FDA's new framework.

Eli Lilly bets big on psychedelic medicine — Lilly's acquisition of atai Beckley closed Sept. 11, bringing three clinical-stage psychedelic candidates in-house just days after FDA published its new trial framework.

Court upholds marijuana's Schedule III reclassification — The D.C. Circuit left the medical marijuana rescheduling order in effect on Sept. 9, rejecting opponents' bid to block the shift out of Schedule I.

Hemp industry wins extra runway on THC ban — GOP lawmakers filed amendments aimed at regulating rather than recriminalizing hemp THC products, building on the recent delay of the federal ban to Dec. 11.
